easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Son of man, cause Jerusalem to know her abominations.”
easy.q: To whom was Ezekiel commanded to make known Jerusalem's abominations?

easy.explanation: She is portrayed as a newborn child cast out into the open field.
easy.q: How is Jerusalem first portrayed?

easy.explanation: The Lord said twice, “Live.”
easy.q: What did the Lord say to Jerusalem when she was polluted in her blood?

answers: That she was born into royalty
medium.explanation: The list emphasizes that no one cared for her.
medium.q: What do the things not done for the infant—washing, salting, and swaddling—show?

medium.explanation: She multiplied, grew, and became mature.
medium.q: What happened to Jerusalem after the Lord told her to live?

answers: A time of maturity and covenant relationship
medium.explanation: It refers to the time when Jerusalem had matured and was ready for covenant relationship.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “the time of love” indicate?

answers: She was abandoned at first but protected afterward
She was rich at first but poor afterward
She was strong at first but weak afterward
challenge.explanation: She was cast out in the field, but the Lord found, preserved, and protected her.
challenge.q: What major contrast appears in Jerusalem's beginning?

challenge.explanation: Covering her nakedness signifies protection and entering into covenant.
challenge.q: What does the Lord's spreading his skirt over Jerusalem signify?

challenge.explanation: The Lord swore to her and entered into a covenant with her.
challenge.q: What completes the rescue described in this passage?

short_answers.question: What did the Lord see when he passed by Jerusalem?
short_answers.answer: She was polluted in her own blood.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 6 says the Lord saw her polluted in her blood.

short_answers.question: What was not cut when Jerusalem was born?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 4 says her navel was not cut.

short_answers.question: Whose did Jerusalem become?
short_answers.explanation: After the covenant, the Lord says, “Thou becamest mine.”

paragraphs.title: The Splendor and Royal Status God Gave

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Then washed I thee with water.”
easy.q: What did the Lord wash Jerusalem with?

answers: Fine linen, silk, and broidered work
easy.explanation: The passage names fine linen, silk, and broidered work.
easy.q: Which materials are mentioned among Jerusalem's clothing?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “thou didst prosper into a kingdom.”
easy.q: What status did Jerusalem attain?

answers: He destroyed, expelled, and punished her
He washed, clothed, adorned, and enriched her
He hid, weakened, and frightened her
medium.explanation: The Lord washed, clothed, adorned, fed, and enriched Jerusalem.
medium.q: What general sequence describes the Lord's actions for Jerusalem?

medium.explanation: Her renown went forth among the heathen, and she prospered into a kingdom.
medium.q: How did the splendor given to Jerusalem affect her status?

medium.explanation: The chain was placed around her neck as jewelry.
medium.q: What is a “chain” in the description of Jerusalem's adornment?

answers: To the comeliness the Lord put upon her
challenge.explanation: Her beauty was perfect through the Lord's comeliness placed upon her.
challenge.q: To what does the passage attribute Jerusalem's splendor?

answers: Her beauty caused her renown to spread among the heathen
Her beauty caused her to hide
challenge.explanation: Her renown went forth among the heathen because of her beauty.
challenge.q: What connection is made between Jerusalem's beauty and her reputation?

answers: The Lord gave her abundance and honor
challenge.explanation: The gifts portray abundance, honor, and preparation for royal status.
challenge.q: What do the many garments, jewels, and foods imply?

short_answers.question: What was placed upon Jerusalem's head?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 12 mentions a beautiful crown upon her head.

short_answers.question: What foods did Jerusalem eat?
short_answers.explanation: These foods are listed in verse 13.

short_answers.question: Among whom did Jerusalem's renown go forth?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 14 says her renown went forth among the heathen.

easy.explanation: The passage says, “thou didst trust in thine own beauty.”
easy.q: What did Jerusalem trust in?

answers: High places decked with divers colours
easy.explanation: She took her garments and decked her high places with them.
easy.q: What did Jerusalem make from her garments?

easy.explanation: The passage says she sacrificed her sons and daughters.
easy.q: What did Jerusalem do with her children?

answers: She returned them to the Lord
She used them only to help the poor
medium.explanation: She used the gold, silver, garments, oil, incense, and food before idols.
medium.q: How did Jerusalem use the gifts she had received from the Lord?

answers: She set it before idols for a sweet savour
She cast it into the sea
medium.explanation: She placed the food before idols as a sweet savour.
medium.q: What did Jerusalem do with the food given to her?

medium.explanation: The word refers to detestable sinful actions, especially idolatry and child sacrifice.
medium.q: What does “abominations” mean in this passage?

answers: She turned the good gifts against the One who gave them
She kept the gifts for herself
challenge.explanation: The gifts from the Lord were used in the worship of idols.
challenge.q: What made Jerusalem's misuse of the Lord's gifts especially serious?

answers: Trust in beauty led to idolatry and child sacrifice
challenge.explanation: Trusting in beauty led to high places, idols, offerings, and sacrificed children.
challenge.q: What progression appears in verses 15–22?

answers: That they belonged to the Lord and were not hers to sacrifice
That they were not born to Jerusalem
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes the Lord's claim upon the children and the seriousness of giving them to idols.
challenge.q: What does “my children” emphasize regarding Jerusalem's children?

short_answers.question: What did Jerusalem make from the Lord's gold and silver?
short_answers.explanation: She made images from the gold and silver given to her.

short_answers.question: What did she set before the idols as a sweet savour?
short_answers.answer: Her meat, including fine flour, oil, and honey.
short_answers.explanation: She offered the food the Lord had given her.

short_answers.question: Through what were the children made to pass?
short_answers.explanation: The passage says they were delivered to pass through the fire.

paragraphs.title: The Expansion of Prostitution and Foreign Alliances

easy.explanation: The passage names Egypt and Assyria, as well as other foreign peoples.
easy.q: With whom is Jerusalem described as committing fornication?

easy.explanation: The passage repeatedly says she was not satisfied.
easy.q: Was Jerusalem satisfied by her many alliances?

answers: She gave gifts and paid others
easy.explanation: She gave gifts to her lovers and hired them to come to her.
easy.q: Unlike an ordinary harlot who receives hire, what did Jerusalem do?

answers: Insatiability and repeated appeals to foreign nations
A desire to help the poor
medium.explanation: She turned to Egypt, Assyria, Canaan, and Chaldea but remained unsatisfied.
medium.q: What led to the expansion of Jerusalem's prostitution?

answers: Jerusalem paid others to attract them instead of receiving payment
Jerusalem received payment from every nation
medium.explanation: The passage says she was contrary because she gave a reward instead of receiving one.
medium.q: What is the point of comparing Jerusalem with an ordinary harlot?

answers: Payment or gifts used to attract lovers
medium.explanation: It refers to gifts or payment given to persuade lovers to come to her.
medium.q: What does “hire” mean in this context?

answers: She appealed to many nations without becoming satisfied
She turned to only one nation and was content
challenge.explanation: She sought Egypt, Assyria, Canaan, and Chaldea, yet remained unsatisfied.
challenge.q: What repeated pattern appears in Jerusalem's dealings with the nations?

answers: That her sin was public and widespread
That her sin was completely hidden
challenge.explanation: The repeated locations show that the sin was extensive and openly practiced.
challenge.q: What does building high places in every street show?

answers: It shows that Jerusalem behaved unusually even compared with a harlot
It describes her return to the covenant
challenge.explanation: She did not merely receive payment; she paid others to come to her.
challenge.q: How does the phrase “thou art contrary” strengthen the criticism?

short_answers.question: Which nation was described as Jerusalem's neighbor in this passage?
short_answers.explanation: The passage calls Egypt Jerusalem's neighbor.

short_answers.question: Why could Jerusalem not be satisfied?
short_answers.answer: Because she was insatiable and multiplied her foreign alliances.
short_answers.explanation: Her repeated alliances never satisfied her.

short_answers.question: Whom did Jerusalem hire to come to her?
short_answers.explanation: She gave gifts and hired her lovers to come from every side.

paragraphs.title: Judgment and Humiliation by the Former Lovers

answers: Her lovers and the nations she pursued
Only the poor of the city
easy.explanation: The Lord would gather her lovers and those she had loved or hated.
easy.q: Who would gather against Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The Lord says he would discover her nakedness before them.
easy.q: What would be exposed before the nations?

easy.explanation: The nations would throw down and break down her high places.
easy.q: What would happen to her high places?

answers: The nations she pursued become instruments of judgment
medium.explanation: Her former lovers are gathered against her and become agents of judgment.
medium.q: What connection exists between Jerusalem's sins and her punishment?

answers: Exposure, destruction of high places, and removal of clothing
medium.explanation: The judgment includes exposing her, destroying her high places, and stripping her.
medium.q: What does the humiliation include?

answers: The Lord's anger will subside after judgment
The Lord forgot the sin without judgment
medium.explanation: After judgment, the Lord's fury and jealousy will cease.
medium.q: What does “I will be quiet, and will be no more angry” mean?

answers: Those whose favor she sought become the agents of her judgment
challenge.explanation: The nations she pursued gather against her and expose her shame.
challenge.q: What ironic reversal occurs in the role of Jerusalem's lovers?

answers: Removing the places of sin symbolizes the end of her sinful practice
challenge.explanation: The judgment destroys the high places and stops her from playing the harlot.
challenge.q: How does destroying the high places relate to ending Jerusalem's prostitution?

answers: She forgot her former condition and the mercy shown to her
She remembered all the Lord's mercies
challenge.explanation: She forgot her neglected beginning and the Lord's rescue of her.
challenge.q: What does forgetting the days of her youth indicate?

short_answers.question: What would the nations see?
short_answers.explanation: The Lord would discover her nakedness before them.

short_answers.question: What would the nations do to Jerusalem's houses?
short_answers.answer: They would burn them with fire.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 41 says they would burn her houses with fire.

short_answers.question: What would Jerusalem no longer give?
short_answers.explanation: The Lord says she would give no hire any more.

paragraphs.title: The Mother and Sisters: Samaria and Sodom

easy.explanation: The passage says, “your mother was an Hittite.”
easy.q: Who was Jerusalem's mother according to the passage?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “your father an Amorite.”
easy.q: Who was Jerusalem's father?

easy.explanation: Samaria is the elder sister and Sodom the younger sister.
easy.q: Which cities are presented as Jerusalem's sisters?

answers: Samaria is on her left and Sodom on her right
medium.explanation: Samaria dwells at Jerusalem's left hand and Sodom at her right hand.
medium.q: Where are Jerusalem's sisters located in relation to her?

answers: She sinned less than they did
She was no different from them
She was more corrupted than they were
medium.explanation: The passage says Jerusalem was corrupted more than they in all her ways.
medium.q: How are Jerusalem's sins compared with those of Samaria and Sodom?

medium.explanation: Pride is listed among Sodom's sins.
medium.q: What does “pride” describe in the account of Sodom?

answers: Her sins were more numerous and serious than theirs
challenge.explanation: Jerusalem's greater wickedness made Samaria and Sodom appear righteous by comparison.
challenge.q: Why are Jerusalem's sisters said to be justified by her actions?

answers: She did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy
challenge.explanation: The passage says she did not strengthen the hand of the poor and needy.
challenge.q: What social sin is explicitly named in Sodom's description?

answers: The comparison increases Jerusalem's guilt by showing the sins of the others
challenge.explanation: The comparison shows that Jerusalem sinned even more than the cities already condemned.
challenge.q: What is the purpose of comparing Jerusalem with her sisters?

short_answers.question: Where was Samaria located relative to Jerusalem?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 46 places Samaria at her left hand.

short_answers.question: What three conditions are listed among Sodom's sins?
short_answers.answer: Pride, fulness of bread, and abundance of idleness.
short_answers.explanation: These are named in verse 49.

short_answers.question: How much of Jerusalem's sins had Samaria committed?
short_answers.explanation: The passage says Samaria had not committed half of Jerusalem's sins.

paragraphs.title: Shame, Restoration, and the Return of the Sisters

easy.explanation: The passage mentions the captivity of all three cities.
easy.q: Whose captivity did the Lord promise to bring again?

easy.explanation: She would bear her shame and be confounded.
easy.q: What would Jerusalem bear before restoration?

answers: They would return to their former estate
easy.explanation: The passage says they would return to their former estate.
easy.q: What would happen to Samaria and Sodom?

medium.explanation: Jerusalem must bear her shame and recognize the seriousness of her actions.
medium.q: What moral condition precedes Jerusalem's restoration?

answers: She will be ashamed when she sees sisters regarded as less sinful restored
She will rejoice because her sisters disappear
medium.explanation: Their restoration highlights Jerusalem's guilt and causes her to be confounded.
medium.q: How is the restoration of the sisters connected with Jerusalem's shame?

medium.explanation: It means a return to their former condition.
medium.q: What does “their former estate” mean?

answers: Restoration is promised, but it does not remove the need to acknowledge guilt
challenge.explanation: The Lord promises restoration while still requiring Jerusalem to bear her shame.
challenge.q: What tension exists between restoration and shame?

answers: Restoration is not limited to Jerusalem
The sisters will only be punished
challenge.explanation: The promise includes all three cities.
challenge.q: What does mentioning Sodom and Samaria show about the extent of restoration?

answers: She would see that even those considered sinful were restored while she bore greater guilt
She would refuse to recognize them
challenge.explanation: Their restoration would emphasize the seriousness of Jerusalem's own sins.
challenge.q: Why could the return of the sisters deepen Jerusalem's shame?

short_answers.question: What would Jerusalem bear?
short_answers.explanation: The passage repeatedly says she would bear her shame.

short_answers.question: To what estate would Sodom and Samaria return?
short_answers.explanation: Both sisters are said to return to their former estate.

short_answers.question: What did Jerusalem's pride prevent her from mentioning?
short_answers.explanation: Sodom was not mentioned by Jerusalem's mouth in the day of her pride.

easy.explanation: The Lord says he will remember his covenant with her in the days of her youth.
easy.q: Which covenant did the Lord remember?

easy.explanation: He promises to establish an everlasting covenant.
easy.q: What covenant would the Lord establish with Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “thou shalt know that I am the Lord.”
easy.q: What would Jerusalem know as a result of the covenant?

answers: He remembers the covenant, establishes an everlasting covenant, and makes atonement
He ends all relationship with the sisters
medium.explanation: The Lord remembers the former covenant, establishes an everlasting one, and is pacified toward her.
medium.q: What actions does the Lord take at the end of the chapter?

answers: She will remember and be ashamed
medium.explanation: She will remember her ways, be confounded, and be ashamed.
medium.q: What will Jerusalem do after the Lord is pacified toward her?

answers: The Lord will remain faithful to his covenant promise
The Lord will destroy the city
The Lord will conceal the city
medium.explanation: The statement expresses the Lord's faithfulness in remembering and renewing the covenant.
medium.q: What does “I will remember my covenant” mean in this context?

answers: The covenant shows mercy, while shame shows recognition of guilt
The covenant proves there was no sin
challenge.explanation: The Lord shows covenant mercy while Jerusalem must remember and acknowledge her sin.
challenge.q: How do covenant remembrance and shame fit together?

answers: She receives a renewed responsibility within a restored relationship, not because of her former covenant
She receives them in order to rule over them
The sisters disappear from the story
challenge.explanation: The restored relationship is granted as part of God's renewed covenant, not because Jerusalem earned it.
challenge.q: What is signified by the sisters being given to Jerusalem as daughters?

answers: Jerusalem remembers, is ashamed, and no longer boasts
challenge.explanation: The final verse connects atonement with remembrance, shame, and silence.
challenge.q: What is the final result of the Lord's atonement?

short_answers.question: What kind of covenant would the Lord establish?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 60 explicitly names an everlasting covenant.

short_answers.question: What would Jerusalem receive as sisters?
short_answers.answer: Sodom and Samaria would be given to her as daughters.
short_answers.explanation: The Lord says she would receive her elder and younger sisters as daughters.

short_answers.question: What would Jerusalem never do any more because of her shame?
short_answers.explanation: She would never open her mouth any more because of her shame.
